arguments.value: This agreement is between iBio Inc. and Beijing CC-Pharming Ltd. It sets up a long-term collaboration for joint research and development of biopharmaceutical products, with each project to be handled under a separate statement of work. iBio grants CC-Pharming a limited, nonexclusive license to use iBio’s plant-based protein technology only to manufacture, process, prepare, and seek regulatory approval for products in China, and not to export products or use the technology in any other country. The first project is a plant-made rituximab product, and iBio will provide technology transfer, development support, facility design consulting, training, quality system design, and regulatory planning services. CC-Pharming must make milestone-based payments to iBio as project deliverables are completed. Inventions made solely by one party belong to that party, while inventions made jointly belong to both parties, with patent costs shared equally. Copyrights follow the same general rule, with jointly created materials jointly owned. Both parties must keep confidential information secret, and either party may negotiate a commercial license for newly disclosed inventions or copyrighted materials within the stated time limits. The agreement’s term begins when the last party signs and continues for [***], and any signed statement of work can continue beyond expiration or termination if its own performance period extends further. The agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Texas, with disputes to be brought only in Texas, including U.S. federal court if there is jurisdiction.
